step1_summary: Chief complaint: Acute sensation of chest tightness for ~3 hours.
Current symptoms: Mild shortness of breath (worse on stair-climbing, not at rest), wheeze, non-productive cough; recent 1-week history of viral “cold” with sore throat & runny nose now improving.
Symptom onset/duration/severity: Began 3 h ago; no frank chest pain, mainly “tightness,” feels unable to take full breath; no hemoptysis, no fever mentioned.
Aggravating/alleviating factors: Worse with exertion; no medication taken because inhalers ran out 1 week ago.
Past medical history: Physician-diagnosed asthma since childhood (severe exacerbation requiring intubation age 16–17); allergic rhinitis/hay fever; childhood eczema, milk-protein allergy.
Medications: Salbutamol (Ventolin) SABA inhaler & beclomethasone (Clenil Modulite) ICS inhaler, both out of supply for ~1 week. No other drugs.
Allergies: No drug allergies; environmental allergy to dust.
Family history: Father with asthma, mother with eczema.
Social history: 26-year-old university student; no smoking/alcohol data given; currently away at university.
Vital signs/exam: None provided (tele-consult); patient not short of breath at rest; able to converse in full sentences.
Investigations: None performed in call (no peak-flow, labs or imaging).

V: Pulmonary embolism – sudden chest tightness & mild dyspnea could rarely be PE, especially if recent immobilisation/flight (not stated).
I: Viral acute bronchitis / upper-respiratory infection – 1-week ‘cold,’ lingering cough & wheeze.
Community-acquired pneumonia – post-viral infection could progress, causing chest tightness & SOB (no sputum, but worth consideration).
N: Mediastinal / bronchial tumors – very unlikely in 26 y but chronic wheeze/cough could rarely be first sign.
D: Early COPD or bronchiectasis – smoking status unknown; age makes this less likely.
I2: Medication non-adherence / withdrawal – stopping inhaled corticosteroid could precipitate asthma flare.
C: Congenital airway abnormality (e.g., tracheomalacia) – longstanding asthma picture makes this less likely but conceivable.
A: Acute allergic asthma flare – environmental allergen exposure causing bronchospasm.
T: Spontaneous pneumothorax – sudden chest tightness in young men, but absence of acute pleuritic pain & normal speech makes this less likely.
E: Anxiety/panic attack – chest tightness & SOB without objective findings can be due to anxiety.

step3_ranked_ddx.diagnosis: Acute asthma exacerbation precipitated by viral URI and lapse in controller therapy
step3_ranked_ddx.explanation: History of asthma, recent viral infection, stopped both SABA & ICS for a week, now presents with classic wheeze, cough, chest tightness and mild exertional dyspnea.

step3_ranked_ddx.diagnosis: Viral acute bronchitis with reactive airways (post-infectious cough/wheeze)
step3_ranked_ddx.explanation: Ongoing post-viral symptoms and cough could independently cause airway irritation and transient bronchospasm even in non-asthmatics; overlaps with asthma flare.
URI progression is a possibility; pneumonia can produce chest discomfort & dyspnea but lack of productive cough, fever or pleuritic pain lowers probability.
Acute chest tightness & SOB could signify PE, yet age, absence of risk factors, tachycardia, pleuritic pain or hemoptysis make it less likely.

step4_evidence.diagnosis: Acute asthma exacerbation precipitated by viral URI and lapse in controller therapy
supporting_evidence: Known asthma with prior severe exacerbation requiring intubation.
Has been without both maintenance (ICS) and rescue (SABA) inhalers for 1 week.
Current wheeze, chest tightness, exertional SOB typical of bronchospasm.
Recent viral URI is common trigger.
Improved when resting, no chest pain, suggests bronchoconstriction rather than cardiopulmonary ischemia.
opposing_evidence: No objective data (peak flow, O2 sat) provided; not overtly in distress at rest which may suggest mild flare.

step4_evidence.diagnosis: Viral acute bronchitis with reactive airways
supporting_evidence: Had ‘cold’ last week with ongoing cough.
Non-productive cough, mild wheeze common in viral bronchitis.
Young age; viral infections common at university.
opposing_evidence: Wheeze and tightness more readily explained by underlying asthma, especially given medication lapse.
No fever or systemic illness reported.

supporting_evidence: Follows viral URI; cough persisting >1 week.
Chest tightness & SOB can accompany pneumonia.
opposing_evidence: Afebrile, no sputum, no pleuritic pain, able to speak full sentences, symptoms only 3 h in severity spike.

supporting_evidence: Acute onset chest tightness with mild dyspnea.
opposing_evidence: No tachypnea at rest, no pleuritic pain, no leg pain/swelling, no clotting risk factors mentioned, wheeze points more toward airway cause.
